Sound Familiar?

Common Osteopathic Medicine Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

OMT billed with wrong body region count, under-coding when multiple regions were treated.

PMEX counts the documented body regions from the treatment note and applies the correct 98925 to 98929 code.

E/M and OMT billed on the same day without modifier 25 on the E/M, payer bundles into OMT.

PMEX applies modifier 25 to every E/M billed with OMT on the same day and confirms separate documentation supports both.

OMT body regions not documented specifically in the clinical note, claim denied on audit.

PMEX reviews OMT notes for specific body region documentation before coding any OMT encounter.

Prior authorization not obtained before an extended OMT treatment course begins.

PMEX manages OMT prior authorization for commercial payers with visit limits before the series begins.

Medicare OMT claim denied because the diagnosis code does not establish somatic dysfunction.

PMEX confirms the somatic dysfunction diagnosis code (M99.00 to M99.09) is present on every Medicare OMT claim.

OMT and chiropractic billed under the same diagnosis without distinguishing the DO approach.

PMEX applies the osteopathic-specific documentation and coding that distinguishes OMT from chiropractic manipulation.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Osteopathic Medicine Billing

Osteopathic practices lose 16 to 26 percent of revenue to body region under-coding, E/M bundling errors, and somatic dysfunction diagnosis gaps.

PATTERN 01

OMT Under-Coded, Body Regions Not Fully Counted

DO treats cervical, thoracic, lumbar, and sacral regions. Clinical note documents all four regions. 98927 (3 to 4 body regions, $90) should be submitted. Billing team submits 98926 (1 to 2 regions, $65). $25 per visit under-coded. At 200 monthly OMT visits, that is $5,000 monthly in systematic under-coding.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX counts the body regions documented in the clinical note before selecting the OMT CPT code. 98925 (1 to 2), 98926 (3 to 4), 98927 (5 to 6), 98928 (7 to 8), and 98929 (9 or more) are applied per the documented treatment record.

PATTERN 02

E/M Bundled into OMT, Modifier 25 Missing

Patient presents with a new musculoskeletal complaint. DO performs an E/M evaluation and provides OMT. E/M submitted without modifier 25. Payer bundles the E/M into the OMT reimbursement. $65 to $130 in E/M revenue lost when the documentation clearly supports a distinct evaluation service.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX applies modifier 25 to the E/M on every encounter where OMT and an E/M are billed together, and confirms the clinical note documents a separately identifiable evaluation that would have been provided regardless of whether OMT was performed.

PATTERN 03

Medicare OMT Denied, Somatic Dysfunction Diagnosis Missing

OMT claim submitted for cervical and lumbar treatment. Primary diagnosis: low back pain (M54.51). Medicare requires a somatic dysfunction diagnosis code (M99.01 for cervical, M99.03 for lumbar) alongside the pain diagnosis. Claim denied for missing somatic dysfunction code.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX confirms that somatic dysfunction diagnosis codes (M99.00 to M99.09) are present on every Medicare OMT claim, linked to the specific body regions treated, alongside any associated pain or musculoskeletal diagnosis codes.

Questions

Osteopathic Medicine Billing Questions Answered

OMT codes 98925 to 98929 are determined by the number of body regions treated. Body regions include head, cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacral, pelvic, lower extremity, upper extremity, and rib cage. We count the documented regions from the clinical note.

Yes, when the E/M is a separately identifiable service documented independently from the OMT treatment decision. We apply modifier 25 to the E/M and confirm the documentation supports a distinct evaluation service.

Medicare requires a somatic dysfunction diagnosis code (M99.00 to M99.09) corresponding to the body region treated. We confirm the somatic dysfunction code is present and linked to the treated region on every Medicare OMT claim.

Some commercial payers require prior authorization for OMT beyond a certain number of visits per year. We manage authorization before the series begins and track visit counts against the authorized limit.

Non-OMT telehealth visits (E/M, consultations) are billed with modifier 95 and the correct place of service code. OMT cannot be delivered via telehealth. We confirm visit type before applying telehealth billing.

Within 30 days, with OMT body region counting workflows and Medicare somatic dysfunction coding active from day one.
